description:
APOGEE is a team of passionate innovators participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge, driven by curiosity, creativity, and a shared vision of solving real-world challenges through technology.

For this challenge, our team is working on Astronaut Health Monitoring Software, a solution designed to help astronauts monitor their health during space missions, track vital signs, identify potential health risks, and receive guidance for maintaining their well-being in space.
summary: The astronauts live away from the hospitals and experience unique body modifications such as changes in heartbeat, disruption of sleep, fatigue, and radiation exposure, which are rarely observed by the physicians here on Earth. Our Space App named AETHER attempts to monitor all these conditions within a single dashboard. There are five components to the application. Astronaut maintains the profile of the crew members. Evaluation analyzes the symptoms provided and identifies possible causes. Health monitors the incoming vital signs while the Tracking module analyzes the past data and estimates future values. Whenever the values recorded by Health breach the threshold, the emergency alarm is raised, and Emergency Response starts the incident..
details:
Link to code repository: https://github.com/N0one123/AETHER

AETHER is a web platform that brings together the health monitoring of astronauts in one place. It is made up of five parts that work together.

AETHER is a connected astronaut health-monitoring platform. It brings crew profiles, symptom evaluation, live health monitoring, trend analysis and emergency response into one web system.

How It Works – Key Technical Innovations

Five-Core Modular Architecture: Astronaut manages profiles, Evaluation turns reported symptoms into possible explanations, Health monitors measurements, Tracking analyses history, and Emergency Response manages incidents. A Communication System passes events between Cores, and SQLite stores the records.

Synthetic Health Simulation: We can’t connect a real astronaut to sensors, so a Simulation Engine generates changing readings (heart rate, SpO₂, temperature, fatigue) from user-entered starting values. All simulated data is labelled synthetic.

Accelerated Simulated Clock: A separate clock runs at 1×, 2×, 5× or 10×, with pause, resume and reset, so hours of mission data play out in minutes.

Automatic Alerting: Health checks readings against warning thresholds. When one is crossed, or radiation climbs too high, Emergency Response opens a prioritised incident for qualified personnel and tracks it to resolution.

Trend Analysis: Tracking compares stored readings, finds patterns and estimates what may come next.

Benefits and Impact

Astronauts can’t always get immediate medical attention, so early warning matters. AETHER raises alerts automatically and shows how measurements change over time. We aim to make long missions safer while supporting, not replacing, medical staff.

Tools

Python, FastAPI, SQLite, HTML, CSS, Jinja2, NumPy, Pandas and Plotly. No special hardware is needed, just a browser.

Creativity

Instead of only displaying numbers, AETHER links symptoms, readings, history and emergency response in one workflow. Its accelerated synthetic simulation lets anyone watch a mission unfold without a real sensor.

Factors We Considered

Synthetic data is always labelled; Evaluation gives possible explanations, not diagnoses; predictions are estimates; and modular Cores keep the system easy to expand.

Use of 'SI'

ChatGPT:-used for gathering information and research
